correctness.rationale: Alphabet relabeling to canonical restricted-growth digits 0,1,2 is bijective on symbol-permutation classes and preserves all LCS. Weakly admissible words (20LCS<=9L for every pair) are prefix closed. Appending a letter adds only new right-endpoint pair tests, so the recurrence tests every canonical word exactly once. I independently implemented a fresh dynamic-programming LCS exhaustive recurrence: length counts through n=33 match repository certificate for all 33 levels, with precisely 10 survivors at n=32 and 0 at n=33. I independently tested every pair of the explicit witness 01020120212012101201020120212012; strict minimum margin 9L-20LCS is 1. Inspected the actual 30-extension certificate and two source LCS implementations (DP and bit-parallel). The finite exhaustive classification plus prefix inheritance, not sampling, proves all n>=33 impossible. For epsilon<=.9 the same obstruction rules out unbounded ternary strings; it does not determine epsilon>.9.
